prompts.text: Our entire group gets to write one rule for a new city. What's the first rule to cause an argument?
What harmless activity should require a very dramatic official licence in an imaginary city?
A city where everyone must wear a hat on Mondays or one where greetings must be sung?
Any city with a public holiday devoted to naps would instantly become a tourist destination.
Tell me about a real rule you've encountered that sounded so strange it could have been invented for a comedy.
If street signs offered personal advice, walking around town would take considerably longer.
The mayor announces that all roundabouts must have a mascot. What animal does our group nominate?
Who among us would volunteer to become the minister responsible for making life slightly more interesting?
A neighbourhood with public hammocks or one with free birthday cake at the town hall?
The best imaginary city would have a complaints department that gives out biscuits.
Which completely useless superpower could somebody in this group somehow turn into a career?
You can make any spoon glow for ten seconds. How do we use your power to save the day?
Always knowing which queue is shortest or being able to locate one missing sock each morning?
Someone with the power to understand pigeons would eventually be pulled into their complicated politics.
The ability to control the volume of nearby alarm clocks is far more dangerous than it first appears.
Tell us about a time you wished you had a very specific power for an embarrassingly small problem.
Our powers only work when we're singing badly. What could our superhero team possibly accomplish?
What superpower would be a terrible idea to give the most competitive person here?
The power to instantly peel oranges or the power to make cold tea the perfect temperature?
A superhero who can summon exact change should never have to buy their own bus ticket.
We're stranded on an island with a working supermarket but no staff. What happens on day one?
What job would you give yourself if this group had to run an island for a month?
An island where the only animals are confident chickens or one full of extremely polite monkeys?
Tell us about a real holiday mishap that felt like the beginning of a strange survival story.
Our group's first island election would be delayed by disagreement over what to call the island.
Someone will start a snack-based economy before anybody figures out where to sleep.
The island's only radio station plays one song on repeat. Who gets appointed music director?
Which person here would attempt to domesticate a wild coconut?
Building one luxurious shared treehouse or giving everybody a tiny separate hut?
A five-star island resort run by this group would run out of towels before breakfast.
We travel to the year 1880 but are only allowed to bring one modern kitchen gadget. What's our choice?
Which everyday inconvenience from fifty years ago would most quickly defeat this group?
Spending a day in the future without understanding the slang or in the past without knowing local manners?
Time travellers would be much less impressive if they kept asking everyone for Wi-Fi passwords.
Tell us about an old photograph that made you wonder how people managed something ordinary.
The most confusing part of future history lessons would probably be explaining our internet jokes.
We accidentally teach somebody in ancient times a modern nursery rhyme. What bizarre legend develops?
Who here would be least believable when trying to explain a smartphone to somebody from 1800?
Meeting your grandparents at your current age or interviewing your great-grandchildren about their favourite snacks?
A time machine with a luggage allowance would start more arguments than it solved.
Every object in the kitchen can speak for one hour. Which one has the most complaints?
If your shoes could tell stories, what would they reveal about your typical Saturday?
A fridge that gives advice or a mirror that reviews your outfits like a fashion critic?
Tell us about losing an object so often you almost felt it was hiding from you deliberately.
A talking alarm clock would be unbearable unless it came with a snooze button for its opinions.
The oldest chair in a house would probably have the most entertaining stories about visitors.
Your suitcase refuses to leave for holiday until you pack properly. How does the negotiation go?
Which object at this gathering would immediately become the group gossip?
A pen that refuses to write lies or a phone charger that only works when you say please?
Talking household appliances would be considerably less fun after the washing machine discovered sarcasm.
We're invited to apply for imaginary jobs such as Cloud Sculptor and Chief Biscuit Inspector. Which do you choose?
What made-up job sounds ridiculous but might genuinely make somebody happy?
Professional queue entertainer or certified nap-quality inspector?
In a world of strange professions, somebody would still manage to complain about Monday morning meetings.
A job title containing the word 'Supreme' should automatically come with an unnecessarily large hat.
Tell us about a real job title you heard that made you ask what the person actually does.
Our team opens a consultancy teaching pets good manners. Which member becomes the CEO?
Who among us is best suited to being an official tester of comfortable park benches?
Inventing names for new colours or judging the sound of closing car doors?
The imaginary job of Professional Birthday Reminder might be the only one this group could agree is essential.
Every country must vote on the world's official breakfast food. What argument do we bring to the summit?

relatedThemes: The world votes on tiny decisions

prompts.text: We win a lottery where the prize is free bananas for twenty years. What's our next move?
What's the funniest prize you could receive that would create more problems than it solves?
Unlimited cinema popcorn or a lifetime supply of brightly coloured notebooks?
Tell us about winning a small competition whose prize was stranger than you expected.
Any competition with a mystery prize should be required to provide a warning about storage space.
The winner of a free year's supply of balloons would quickly become everyone's default party planner.
Our group wins a miniature train that only goes around a garden. Who insists it's useful transport?
Which person here would know exactly what to do with a thousand identical rubber ducks?
Winning naming rights to a tiny island or having a new sandwich named after you?
The best lottery prize might be someone else taking responsibility for choosing where to eat.
A friendly alien lands at our table and wants to understand birthday parties. Who volunteers to explain?
What human habit would be hardest to justify to visitors from another planet?
Showing aliens a busy supermarket or taking them to a football match first?
Visitors from space might reasonably assume escalators are a form of leisurely entertainment.
Tell us about a moment you tried explaining something obvious and realised it wasn't obvious at all.
An alien would probably think our habit of naming storms is an attempt at making friends with the weather.
The visitors think umbrellas are ceremonial objects. Do we correct them or organise an impressive demonstration?
Which person in the group should absolutely not be appointed Earth's first ambassador?
Teaching an alien how to queue or how to react to somebody showing you a funny video?
If aliens arrived asking for our finest cuisine, we should probably not let the group chat decide.
We book a mystery holiday and discover the destination is a beautiful town made entirely of miniature buildings. What's the itinerary?
What fictional destination would you choose for a group trip if nobody had to worry about safety or expenses?
A hotel where every room has its own tiny garden or one where breakfast is served by miniature robots?
A travel guide written by this group would contain more snack recommendations than practical directions.
Nobody on a fantasy holiday should be allowed to say, 'Let's just wake up early and see everything.'
Tell us about a holiday where an unexpected attraction became the highlight.
The town we're visiting celebrates an annual Festival of Lost Keys. Do we join the parade?
Who would be most delighted if our hotel turned out to have a secret library behind the lift?
Exploring a floating market in the clouds or a quiet village at the bottom of the sea?
The most magical accommodation still needs somewhere for everybody to charge their phones.
